How to Keep a New Florida Home Maintained Year-Round

Seasonal maintenance tips for Florida's unique climate, from hurricane prep to humidity control.

Florida's climate is tough on homes. The intense sun, high humidity, heavy rains, and occasional hurricanes create unique maintenance challenges. Here's your year-round guide to keeping your Babcock Ranch home in top condition.

Understanding Florida's Seasons

While Florida doesn't have dramatic seasonal changes like northern states, our "seasons" matter for home maintenance:

  • Dry Season (November-April): Lower humidity, less rain, cooler temperatures—ideal for outdoor projects
  • Rainy Season (May-October): Daily afternoon thunderstorms, high humidity, hurricane risk—focus on drainage and moisture control

Monthly Maintenance Tasks

These tasks should happen every month, regardless of season:

HVAC System

  • Change air filters: Monthly changes are essential in Florida. Use high-quality pleated filters and check them even if they say they last 3 months.
  • Inspect outdoor unit: Keep it clear of debris, vegetation, and grass clippings. Maintain 2-3 feet of clearance around the unit.
  • Check condensate drain: Make sure the drain line isn't clogged—a common cause of water damage in Florida homes.

Indoor Air Quality

  • Check humidity levels (ideal: 45-55%)
  • Run exhaust fans during showers and cooking
  • Inspect for signs of mold or mildew in bathrooms and closets
  • Check under sinks for leaks

Exterior Inspection

  • Walk around your home looking for damage, cracks, or wear
  • Check for pest entry points
  • Inspect caulking around windows and doors
  • Look for signs of water intrusion

Spring (March-May)

Spring is your last chance to prepare for the intense summer ahead.

Pre-Summer HVAC Prep

  • Schedule professional maintenance before peak season
  • Have refrigerant levels checked
  • Clean evaporator and condenser coils
  • Test thermostat programming

Landscaping

  • Deep root feeding for trees and shrubs
  • Apply pre-emergent herbicide before summer weeds germinate
  • Adjust irrigation for increasing temperatures
  • Trim trees and shrubs away from the house

Storm Preparation

  • Test generator if you have one
  • Inspect and clean gutters and downspouts
  • Check hurricane shutters or panels
  • Review your hurricane preparedness plan

Summer (June-August)

The most challenging season for Florida homes. Focus on moisture control and hurricane readiness.

Hurricane Season Preparation

  • June 1: Review insurance coverage and document home contents
  • Keep hurricane supplies stocked
  • Monitor weather forecasts regularly
  • Know your evacuation zone and routes

Moisture Management

  • Run dehumidifiers if indoor humidity exceeds 60%
  • Check and clean bathroom exhaust fans
  • Inspect attic for proper ventilation
  • Look for condensation on windows and address causes

Pest Control

  • Keep up with quarterly pest control treatments
  • Check for standing water (mosquito breeding)
  • Inspect for signs of termite activity
  • Seal gaps around utility penetrations

Fall (September-November)

Hurricane season continues through November, but temperatures begin to moderate.

Post-Storm Inspection

  • Inspect roof for missing or damaged shingles
  • Check for water intrusion in attic and ceilings
  • Examine exterior paint and caulking
  • Clean and repair gutters and downspouts

Cooling System Transition

  • Schedule post-summer HVAC maintenance
  • Consider having ducts cleaned if needed
  • Test heating function before you need it
  • Change filters (they work extra hard in summer)

Landscaping

  • Fall is ideal for planting in Florida
  • Reduce irrigation as temperatures drop
  • Fertilize lawn for winter health
  • Plan major landscaping projects for the dry season

Winter (December-February)

Florida's mildest season—perfect for outdoor projects and deep maintenance.

Deep Maintenance

  • Pressure wash exterior surfaces
  • Touch up exterior paint
  • Service garage door and opener
  • Clean dryer vent thoroughly
  • Inspect and clean refrigerator coils

Home Systems

  • Test smoke and carbon monoxide detectors
  • Check and reset GFCI outlets
  • Inspect water heater and flush if needed
  • Have fireplace and chimney inspected if applicable

Major Projects

Winter is the best time for:

  • Exterior painting
  • Roof repairs or replacement
  • Major landscaping installations
  • Hardscaping projects
  • Pool renovations

Babcock Ranch Specific Considerations

Solar Systems

As a solar-powered community, understand your home's solar systems:

  • Keep solar water heater panels clean
  • Monitor system performance through your app or interface
  • Report issues to the utility promptly

HOA and Community Standards

  • Stay current on landscaping requirements
  • Submit architectural change requests before starting projects
  • Keep common areas clean and maintained

Creating Your Maintenance Calendar

The best way to stay on top of maintenance is to create a calendar:

  • Use a digital calendar with recurring reminders
  • Create a home maintenance binder with receipts and warranties
  • Keep a running list of things to address during each season
  • Budget annually for maintenance (typically 1-3% of home value)

Final Thoughts

Regular maintenance protects your investment and prevents costly emergency repairs. In Florida's harsh climate, a proactive approach pays dividends. Start with the monthly basics, follow the seasonal guides, and you'll keep your Babcock Ranch home looking and performing its best for years to come.
